title: ESG reporting perceptions from lecturer perspectives: The case of Vietnamese Universities
content:
by Thi Phuong Dung Nguyen, Ha Dac Viet Nguyen, Ha Phuong Nguyen, Thi Thanh Hong Pham

Higher education institutions play a key role in developing Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) expertise and knowledge. Lecturers are central to translating ESG strategies into educational and organizational outcomes, yet their perceptions of ESG reporting remain under-explored in Vietnam. This study examines individual and institutional factors associated with lecturers’ perceptions of ESG reporting, drawing on the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB), Institutional Theory, Stakeholder Theory, and Diffusion of Innovations (DOI) theory. Survey data from 437 eligible university lecturers in Vietnam were analyzed using PLS-SEM. Results show significant positive associations for innovation policies, sustainability action programs, social pressure, attitude, perceived usefulness, and knowledge, while subjective norm and leadership show no significant direct associations. Academic specialization, included as a control variable, is also positively associated with Lecturers’ perceptions of ESG reporting. Institutional ESG publication significantly negatively associated, suggesting that formal disclosure does not necessarily correspond to favorable individual perceptions, although the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Innovation policies significantly moderate the relationship between subjective norm and lecturers’ perceptions of ESG reporting, while other tested moderating effects are not statistically significant. Overall, the findings highlight the interplay between individual evaluations and institutional conditions in understanding lecturers’ perceptions of ESG reporting in Vietnamese higher education.
author: Thi Phuong Dung Nguyen
